s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive subcutaneous node in the axilla with skin infiltration and episodic pain
salient_findings: Slowly growing subcutaneous node in the right axilla
Progressive infiltration of the overlying skin
Erythematous plaque in the right axilla measuring 5 × 3 cm
Dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement
Tumor cells with basophilic nuclei and scant cytoplasm in an 'Indian file pattern'
key_facts: The patient is a woman in her 60s
The subcutaneous node was first noticed 10 years ago
The node has been slowly growing
The patient experienced swelling in the right axilla during pregnancy over 20 years ago
The swelling disappeared with lactation
The patient experienced mild episodic pain in her right axilla during menstrual cycles
A solitary, indolent, erythematous plaque is present in the right axilla
The plaque measures 5 × 3 cm
Histopathology shows dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement
Tumor cells are diffusely dispersed between collagen bundles and lined up in an 'Indian file pattern'
Tumor cells have basophilic nuclei and scant cytoplasm
Immunohistochemistry is positive for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies
Imaging studies show no evidence of primary or secondary tumors

shortlist.label: Hidradenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathology shows dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat with Indian file pattern, and immunohistochemistry is positive for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies, consistent with apocrine origin

shortlist.label: Apocrine carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Tumor cells have basophilic nuclei and scant cytoplasm, and immunohistochemistry is positive for GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies, suggesting apocrine differentiation

shortlist.label: Mammary analog secretory carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathology shows dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement, and immunohistochemistry is positive for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, and estrogen receptor, consistent with secretory carcinoma

shortlist.label: Syringomatous carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Tumor cells are diffusely dispersed between collagen bundles, and immunohistochemistry is positive for pancytokeratin and cytokeratin 20, suggesting eccrine or apocrine origin

shortlist.label: Secretory carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathology shows dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat, and immunohistochemistry is positive for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, and estrogen receptor, consistent with secretory carcinoma

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a solitary, indolent, erythematous plaque in the right axilla with histopathology showing dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat and positive immunohistochemistry for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies is more consistent with hidradenocarcinoma, a subtype of apocrine gland tumors, which can be considered under the broader category of breast cancer-related tumors like invasive ductal carcinoma.

rejected.label: Apocrine carcinoma
rejected.why: While apocrine features are present, the specific pattern and immunohistochemistry suggest a more specific diagnosis of hidradenocarcinoma.

rejected.label: Mammary analog secretory carcinoma
rejected.why: This diagnosis is less likely due to the specific clinical presentation and histopathological features that more closely align with hidradenocarcinoma.

rejected.label: Syringomatous carcinoma
rejected.why: The histopathological description does not match the typical features of syringomatous carcinoma.

rejected.label: Secretory carcinoma
rejected.why: The clinical and histopathological features, along with the immunohistochemistry results, are not as strongly indicative of secretory carcinoma as they are of hidradenocarcinoma.
